closed_form_proof_ranges.contract: Positivity/polarization and Hilbert completion; bounded isometry extension on arbitrary Hilbert spaces.
Projection, orthogonal double complement and Riesz representation, linear-first, arbitrary H.
Bounded sesquilinear-form representation and adjoints. Rectangular adjoint is the same Riesz proof with target vector fixed; explicit bridge supplied in proposal.
Concrete positivity, kernel square-root identity and closure(range T)=(ker T*)-perp.

Rectangular bounded polar decomposition C=U|C|=|C*|U; U unitary when C is injective with dense range. Construction uses bounded square roots and extension of an isometry, with no closed-form/unbounded-polar theorem.
Bounded Borel calculus, finite vector measures, spectral projections and uniqueness; arbitrary cyclic-sum index.
Closedness, dense squared-integral domains, adjoints and self-adjointness for real functions; actual product domains; graph cutoffs.
Existence and uniqueness of arbitrary self-adjoint spectral resolution via Cayley transform; positive support.
Changes of variable; unique positive square root; exact form pairing; inverse domains equal actual ranges; logarithms and powers.
Unitary/antiunitary transport with domains, reduction and bounded Borel membership/affiliation.
Scalar spectral DCT/cutoffs and strong continuous functional-calculus convergence on bounded self-adjoint nets. Line 301 supplies the Bernstein proof of compact-interval polynomial approximation.
Sequential monotone and real/complex dominated convergence for arbitrary measures; use on finite scalar spectral measures. No general net DCT.
Bicommutant theorem; required only for QF-04 optional algebra application.
Four-unitary linear span and unitary commutation test; only optional algebra application.
Zorn maximal principle from choice, transitive input to SK-03. QF does not use a new Hahn–Banach assumption.

tomita_proof_ranges.contract: Linear-first positivity/polarization/Cauchy–Schwarz, Hilbert completion and extension of bounded maps
Projection/double orthogonal complement and linear-first Riesz Theorems2.1–2.3, including zero functional/zero Hilbert
consumers: TC03 adjoint scalar test and graph double complement

tomita_proof_ranges.contract: Bounded adjoints and scalar pairings; TC03 proves the unbounded conjugate-linear adjoint facts itself
Bessel, Parseval and finite-support expansion for arbitrary orthonormal index sets
Complete ell2(S) coordinate Hilbert spaces and tensor products; square-summable matrices give the Hilbert–Schmidt model
Bicommutant theorem by finite-vector approximation on arbitrary Hilbert spaces, including H=0
Closed nonnegative form representation, intrinsic operator-domain criterion and uniqueness, exact square-root domain and converse
Projection-valued bounded Borel calculus, finite scalar measures and uniqueness
Unbounded squared-integral domains, adjoints, kernels, actual product domains and graph cutoffs
Every self-adjoint operator has a unique spectral resolution, including zero Hilbert and positivity support
Positive square roots and uniqueness; inverse on actual range; powers, form pairing and bounded imaginary-power group
Unitary/antiunitary spectral transport, conjugated scalar coefficients and transported domains
Scalar sequential MCT/DCT without ambient sigma-finiteness; imaginary-power continuity uses finite vector measure and bound4
Hölder/Minkowski, Lp completeness/simple density and linear-first L2 pairing on arbitrary measure spaces
